questions.question: What is National Income?

options.text: It is the money value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year
It is the money value of all goods and services produced in a country in two year
It is the money value of all goods and services produced in a country in ﬁve year
It is the money value of all goods and services produced outside the country in a year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**1**__, i.e. __**It is the money value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year.**__

 
• The total money incurred on all the goods and services produced in a given year in a country is termed as the **national income.**
 
• It can also be defined as the Net National Product minus the indirect taxes and subsidies granted by the government.
 
• **NI = NNP at market prices – Indirect taxes – Subsidies**

questions.question: How is the Net National Product calculated?
questions.solution:
• Net National Product is computed by deducting depreciation from the gross national product.

NNP = GNP – Depreciation

 
• Gross national product(GNP) is the net amount of all the goods and services produced in a country in a given year(GDP) along with the income from abroad.

GNP= GDP + Income from Abroad

questions.question: From which date Indian Constitution came into commencement, completely?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Constitution of India became effective from **26th January 1950**__.
 
• It was developed by a drafting committee chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and was adopted on the 26th November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly of India.

questions.question: How many houses are there in the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India which comprises of the President and houses- the **Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha**__.
 
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the upper house of the Parliament and represents the states and union territories.
 
• Lok Sabha (House of the People) is the lower house of the Parliament and represents the people of India as a whole.

questions.question: Stone tools were ﬁrst found in which period?
questions.solution:
• It was during the Palaeolithic Age that humans began using stone tools for hunting animals and gathering food.
 
• The Palaeolithic Age dates back to 2.6 million years ago and lasted till 12,000 years ago.

questions.question: What were cotton textiles generally named in Europe which were taken by Portuguese from Calicut?
questions.solution:
• The cotton textiles that the Portuguese took back to Europe from India were called ‘Calico’ as it originated in Calicut.
 
• India was the world’s largest producer of cotton textiles in 1750s.
 
• The Portuguese first landed in Calicut (present-day Kerala) and took the cotton textiles to Europe and called them calico.

questions.question: What is the position of Mercury from the Sun among the eight planets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e., __**First**__.

 
• Our Solar system consists of eight planets that revolve around the Sun in imaginary orbits and are bounded by gravitational force.
 
• **Mercury **is the smallest and innermost planet in the Solar System.
 
• **Its orbital period around the Sun of 88 days is the shortest of all the planets in the Solar System.**
 
• The order of the planets from first to last moving away from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

questions.question: What is the zone between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn called?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Torrid zone refers to the hottest central belt of the earth bounded by the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, characterized by a hot climate. It lies between 23 ½° North latitude and 23 ½° South latitude. It is also known as the hottest zone as it is very close to the equator and sun rays fall directly on it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a192f3577d87c0ea91337f773ba9889b3a1d853552e9aadd0adcfc92554b6699.png] 

__
 
• The zone between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn is known as the torrid zone.
 
• There are mainly 3 heat zones on the Earth's surface that arise due to temperature differences. They are -

 
 

 
 
**Zones**__

 
 
 
__**Location**__

 
 
 

 
 
Frigid Zone

 
 
 
Further divided into 2 zones:

 
 
• North frigid zone- between the Arctic Circle 66.5° N and the North Pole 90° N
 
• South frigid zone- between the Antarctic Circle 66.5° S and the South Pole 90° S
 
 
 
 

 
 
Temperate Zone

 
 
 
Further divide into 2 zones:

 
 
• The North temperate zone which is between the Tropic of Cancer 23.5° N and the Arctic Circle 66.5° N
 
• The South temperate zone which is between the Tropic of Capricorn 23.5° S and the Antarctic Circle 66.5° S
 
 
 
 

 
 
Torrid zone

 
 
 
 
• Located between the Tropic of Cancer 23.5° N and the Tropic of Capricorn 23.5° S

questions.question: Which of the following roots are not eaten?
questions.solution:
• Wheat is a grass that is cultivated for its grains and not the roots.
 
• The grains yield white flour which is used in making bread, and other bakery items.
 
• On the other hand, carrot, tapioca, and radish are edible roots.

questions.question: Deficiency of which of the following Vitamins prevents from the clotting of blood?
questions.solution:
__
 
• It is the deficiency of **Vitamin K**__** **which prevents the clotting of blood.
 
• Vitamin K plays an important role in the process of blood clotting as it helps in the formation of Prothrombin and Fibrinogen which are essential blood clotting factors.

 
• Fibrinogen combines with thrombin to form Fibrin which then further combines with the blood corpuscles to form a blood clot.

 

 
 

 Vitamin A
 Night blindness
 
 

 Vitamin E
 Vision problems
 
 

 Vitamin D
 Rickets

questions.question: In humans, ribs are attached to ________.
questions.solution:
• In the human body, the ribs are attached to the sternum in the front and 12 thoracic vertebrae at the back thus making up the ribcage.
 
• The ribcage supports the chest and protects vital organs like the heart and lungs.
 
• There are 12 pairs of ribs out of which, the first 7 pairs are called ‘true ribs’ followed by 3 pairs of ‘false ribs’ and 2 pairs of ‘floating ribs’.

questions.question: The reciprocal of resistance is conductance. If the unit of resistance is ohm, the unit of conductance will be ________.
questions.solution:
• Obstruction to the flow of current is called electrical resistance. Its SI unit is ohm(Ω).
 
• Electrical conductance(G) is defined as the ease with which electric current can pass through a conductor.
 
• It is the reciprocal of resistance, therefore, its SI unit is ohm⁻¹ commonly referred as mho.

questions.question: Minimum energy is required when a body is ________.

options.text: pulled on a plane horizontal surface

questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**:__

__
 
• **Friction force**: When two objects are in contact and one object **moves or intends to move** then an **opposing force** develops between the two surfaces called** frictional force**. The friction force is usually denoted by **“f”**.
 
• Due to **friction force, there is a loss in energy**.
 
• **Energy**: The capacity to do work is called energy.

**EXPLANATION**:__

 
• On a** smooth surface, there is no friction**,** so the loss of energy is zero **on the smooth surface.
 
• **Minimum energy is required when a body is pushed over smooth rollers**. So option 3 is correct.
 
• The more the force applied, the more is the work done.
 
• Since **rolling friction provides the least amount of opposing force**,** less work has to be done hence less energy**.

questions.question: What is the ﬁrst page of a website called?
questions.solution:
• The first page which appears on opening any website is called its home page.
 
• It also provides search box and links which help in navigating to other pages of the site.

questions.question: When sodium reacts with ﬂuorine, ________.

options.text: each ﬂuorine atom loses one electron
each sodium atom gains one electron
fluorine neither gains nor loses an electron
the compound formed is a good conductor of electricity in the molten state

questions.solution:
• When Sodium (Na) reacts with Flourine (F), it forms an ionic bond and becomes sodium flouride (NaF).
 
• The presence of ions makes sodium flouride a good conductor of electricity in the molten state.
 
• Sodium flouride finds its applicatons in metallurgy and is also used as a cleansing agent.

questions.question: Essential component of an amalgam is ________.
questions.solution:
• An alloy of mercury with another metal is called an amalgam.
 
• The alloys are bonded by metallic bonding and depending upon the proportion of mercury present in the alloy, the physical state may be liquid, soft paste or solid.

questions.question: What is the effect of greenhouse gases on the average temperature of the earth’s atmosphere?
questions.solution:
• The greenhouse effect occurs when Earth's atmosphere traps solar radiation because of the presence of certain gases called green house gases.
 
• This results in an overall increase in the average temperature of the earth’s atmosphere.
 
• Some major greenhouse gases are- Carbon dioxide, Methane, Nitrous oxide, Chlorofluorocarbons, etc.

questions.question: Which is a scheme for providing Physical aids and Assisted-living Devices for senior citizens belonging to BPL category?
questions.solution:
• Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is a scheme that was launched to aid senior citizens belonging to the BPL category by providing them with Physical aids and Assisted-living Devices like spectacles, wheelchairs, dentures,etc.
 
• The scheme was launched by the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on 1st April 2017.
 
• The responsibility of providing these aides and their maintenance is given to Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO), a PSU.

questions.question: Who invented Barometer?
questions.solution:
• An instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure, the barometer was invented by Evangelista Torricelli in 1643.
 
• E. Torricelli was an Italian mathematician and physicist and was a student of Galileo Galilei.

questions.question: Which country will host the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup?
questions.solution:
• The 12th edition of the ICC Cricket World Cup will be hosted by England and Wales.
 
• It is scheduled from 30th May 2019 to 14th July 2019.

questions.question: Which art is also known as Greco-Buddhist art?
questions.solution:
• Gandhara Art also popularly known as the Greco-Buddhist art was a mixture of Greek and Buddhist culture.
 
• It flourished under the Kushan empire, present-day northwestern Pakistan and parts of Afghanistan, between 1st century BCE to 5thcentury BCE.

questions.question: Who was/were the last person/persons to be awarded ‘Bharat Ratna’? (for year 2015)

options.text: Both Madan Mohan Malaviya and Atal Bihari Vajpayee

questions.solution:
__
 
• Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya and former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee were the last recipients of the Bharat Ratna.
 
• They were awarded Bharat Ratna in 2015.
 
• Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award in India.
 
• **2019 awardees are Pranab Mukherjee, Nanaji Deshmukh, Bhupen Hazarika.**__

questions.question: Who is the author of book named "A Bend in the River"?
questions.solution:
• V.S Naipaul is the author of the book named "A Bend in the River”.
 
• The book was published in May, 1979 and was also short-listed for the Booker Prize in 1979.
 
• Its story is narrated by an Indian-Muslim shopkeeper, Salim, who observes changes in Africa.

questions.question: The African Nuclear Weapon Free Zone treaty is also called as ________.
questions.solution:
• Signed in 1996, the African Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone treaty is also known as the Pelindaba Treaty.
 
• It came into effect on 15th July 2009.
 
• According to this treaty, the research, development, stockpiling, possession, manufacture, control or stationing of nuclear explosive devices is prohibited in the territory of all parties involved in the treaty.
 
• It also prohibits dumping of radioactive waste in the African zone.

questions.question: Which neighbouring country of India is also known by the name of Burma?
questions.solution:
• Burma also known as Myanmar is a Southeast Asian country located to the east of India.
 
• It is also flanked by Bangladesh to the west, China to the north and Thailand to the east.
 
• In 1989, the name of Burma was officially changed to Myanmar by the military government.
